title: A first global standard on platform work
author: Editorial Desk
summary: The ILO opens negotiations on a convention for platform workers.
body:
In June 2025, the **113th session of the International Labour Conference** held its first discussion on **decent work in the platform economy**. The aim is to negotiate a new international labour standard: a convention supplemented by a recommendation.

## Why this is a big step

Previous ILO standards were written for a world of factories, farms and offices. Digital labour platforms bring algorithmic management, cross-border work and new forms of control. A standard would give governments, platforms and workers a common reference.

## The questions under debate

- **Employment status:** should platform workers be treated as employees, self-employed or a third category?
- **Algorithmic transparency:** the right to know how ratings and pay are decided.
- **Social protection** and occupational safety.
- **Freedom of association** and collective bargaining for platform workers.
- **Data protection.**

## India's position

The Government of India, employers' organisations and trade unions have all been consulted. India has its own framework in the Code on Social Security. BMS has urged that any global standard recognise the realities of developing countries, where platform work is a major source of employment.

## What next

A second discussion at the 2026 Conference is expected to decide whether a convention is adopted. We will follow that in this blog.
